explains: Five ways to get soldiers, side by side. They are not better and worse — they are different bargains, and a realm that survives uses all five. Read this the way you would read the back of a card-game box: the whole strategy is in the columns.

fields.coin: What they cost in money — the cost that is easiest to see and rarely the one that matters.
fields.daysToStand: How long from deciding you want them to having them standing in front of you. The single most underrated column in the table.
fields.quality: How good they are, honestly, including how much they vary.
fields.whoseMenTheyAre: Who they actually belong to and answer to. This is the column that decides whether an order is obeyed, and it is why the same number of men is worth wildly different amounts.
fields.politicalPrice: What taking them costs you in something other than coin. Every source in this table is cheap in one currency and expensive in another.
fields.whenToReachForIt: The situation this source is genuinely the right answer to — so the table teaches a decision rather than merely listing options.

sources.name: The feudal levy
sources.daysToStand: 12 to 30 — the letter, then the gathering, then the march
sources.whoseMenTheyAre: the vassal's. His captain leads them, his loyalty holds them, his grudge poisons them.
sources.politicalPrice: drinks the vessel; calling in the wrong season wrecks his harvest; and when his men die badly it is YOUR blood-debt, not the enemy's.
sources.explains: The backbone of every army you will ever field, and the one that talks back. These men are only yours because their lord says so, and their lord has opinions about you.
sources.whenToReachForIt: Always first. It is free, and everything else on this list is a way of covering what it failed to deliver.

sources.name: The Household
sources.coin: 3 crowns per man per season, forever, war or no war
sources.daysToStand: 0 — they are already standing in your courtyard
sources.politicalPrice: none at all — but it is capped by your treasury, and treasury is grudge-settling money
sources.explains: Your own paid soldiers. No letters, no waiting, no excuses, no grudges — the highest obedience in the game, which you feel every time an order lands. Also the only army you pay for in a season when nothing whatsoever is happening.
sources.whenToReachForIt: When the deadline is short. If the enemy is fourteen days away, the Household is the only army that exists.

sources.name: A free company
sources.coin: 2 crowns a man to contract, then 4 a man a season
sources.daysToStand: 8 to 20 — they must be found and they must ride
sources.politicalPrice: every house that sat idle while you hired foreigners takes a grudge; the Church takes 6 off your legitimacy; unpaid, their treachery climbs 12 a season and they may simply ride off the field
sources.explains: Professional soldiers who will fight for anybody. They are very good at their job and they have no reason at all to die for you. They convert money into men, which is the only escape from a shrinking realm — and they insult every vassal who was not asked.
sources.whenToReachForIt: When your musters are bleeding and your coffer is not. The ladder out of a losing streak that does not require anybody to like you.

sources.name: The town militia
sources.coin: cheap in coin, dear in liberties
sources.daysToStand: 4 to 10 — towns sit on the roads
sources.quality: poor in the open field, stubborn behind a wall
sources.whoseMenTheyAre: the town's. They will not pursue and they do not want to leave their own province.
sources.politicalPrice: a Charter is permanent — a fifth of that town's tax, forever. Levy the same town twice in three years and it riots.
sources.explains: A great many shopkeepers with spears. They arrive faster than anybody because towns are near, they will hold their own wall all day out of sheer bloody-mindedness, and in an open field they are a rumour that has not run away yet.
sources.whenToReachForIt: When you need numbers this month and you are willing to pay for them every year afterwards.

sources.name: The Sworn Order
sources.daysToStand: 15 to 25, and only for a blessed cause
sources.politicalPrice: they come only for a cause your Chaplain has blessed; their obedience is capped at 55 whatever you do; asking them into an unjust war costs 20 legitimacy
sources.explains: Sixty men who will not run away from anything, ever, for nothing. The catch is that they are certain they know God's will better than you do, so at some point in a battle they will do what they think is right instead of what you asked. Resolve 95 and obedience 55 is a very particular kind of nightmare to command.
sources.whenToReachForIt: When the war is genuinely just and you have a Chaplain. They are the reward for keeping the Church happy, and the reason an empty Chaplaincy is the largest invisible hole in most players' armies.

theTradeInOneLine: Free men answer slowly and argue. Paid men answer at once and leave when the money stops. Holy men answer for nothing and answer to somebody else. There is no source that is fast, loyal, good and free, and every campaign you will wish there were.
